name: com.offladder/offladder
title: OffLadder
description: Career coach: test a career, look up or compare jobs and what AI changes, plan your runway.

tools.name: find_career_experiment
tools.description: Finds a small way to try, test or get a feel for a career, job, trade or field before committing to it, for someone weighing whether to quit, retrain or switch into it, e.g. 'how do I know if I'd like UX design', 'try nursing before going back to school', 'test a career change this weekend', 'is product management right for me', 'a cheap way to see if I'd enjoy teaching', 'should I quit my job to become a data analyst', 'how can I try coding before a bootcamp', 'what's it really like to be an electrician'. Works for any named career, including nursing, teaching, law, medicine, electrician, plumbing, welding, HVAC, accounting, marketing, sales, HR, real estate, social work, counselling, pharmacy, policing, paramedic, pilot, software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, cloud and DevOps, AI engineering, UX design, product and project management. Returns one small real-world experiment that can be finished in an evening or a weekend, what is worth noticing, OffLadder's written guide to that job when there is one, and a link to carry on with OffLadder's coach.

career.description: The career, field or kind of work they're curious about, in their words.

tools.name: explore_career_directions
tools.description: Suggests kinds of work that might suit someone, for questions about what to do with their life or which careers fit their interests, strengths, values or past experience, e.g. 'what jobs suit someone who likes fixing things', 'careers for people who love the outdoors', 'what else can I do with my teaching experience', 'jobs for creative people that pay', 'careers that aren't just coding', 'new jobs AI is creating', 'jobs that help with climate change', 'meaningful work in health care without being a doctor', 'I'm good with people and spreadsheets, what fits'. Returns two or three emerging directions of work from OffLadder's library of 24, each with what the days contain and one small way to test it, plus a link to carry on with OffLadder's coach.

interests.description: What they enjoy, are good at or are curious about, in their words.

tools.name: check_career_change_facts
tools.description: Answers factual questions about changing jobs or careers, e.g. 'is it too late to change careers at 40', 'is 50 too old to switch careers', 'how many jobs does the average person have in a lifetime', 'how long do people stay with one employer', 'how many different careers are there', 'will AI make my skills outdated', 'how fast are job skills changing'. Returns exact quotes from primary sources (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, O*NET, World Economic Forum) with links, or says plainly that no checked figure exists, along with OffLadder's own guides on the question and the sources they cite. Never returns an estimate.

question.description: The person's question, in their words.

tools.name: find_career_guide
tools.description: Searches OffLadder's 780 written career guides and returns the closest ones, each with its direct answer, key points, primary sources and a link. Fits a how-to, advice or "what should I do" question about work and careers, e.g. 'how do I tailor my CV to a job description', 'how do I explain a career gap', 'what to do in the first 30 days after a layoff', 'how do I answer tell me about yourself', 'how to negotiate a job offer', 'is a degree worth it', 'what can I do with a psychology degree', 'apprenticeship or university', 'how to get a first job with no experience', 'what jobs will AI replace', 'how to write a cover letter for a career change', 'how to beat applicant tracking systems', 'should I follow up after an interview', 'how to read my first payslip', 'I hate my job but don't know what else to do'. Covers: not knowing what to do next, changing careers at any age, testing a career, layoffs and redundancy, AI and the future of work, jobs of the future, school leavers and students, degrees, apprenticeships, internships, graduate jobs, first jobs, first pay and payslips, CVs and resumes, cover letters, LinkedIn profiles, ATS, application forms and screening questions, interviews, job offers and pay, following up, and work that fits your life, with pages for both the UK and the US.

question.description: The person's question, in their words.

country.description: Where the person is, when known, so guides written for their country come first. Leave out for anywhere else.

tools.name: read_career_guide
tools.description: Returns the full text of one OffLadder career guide as Markdown: the direct answer, key takeaways, every section, worked examples and templates, the questions people also ask, and the sources. Suits someone who wants the step-by-step version of a guide rather than its short answer. Takes the guide's path or offladder.com link, e.g. '/answers/tailor-cv-to-job-description', or the guide's question in words, e.g. 'how do I negotiate a job offer'.

guide.description: The guide's path or offladder.com link, e.g. '/answers/tailor-cv-to-job-description', or its question in words.

tools.name: browse_career_guides
tools.description: Lists every OffLadder career guide on one subject, as questions with links, so someone can see what there is to read before picking one, e.g. 'show me everything on interviews', 'what guides do you have for students', 'reading list for after a layoff', 'what do you have on AI and jobs', 'guides on finding remote work', 'everything about resigning and notice periods'. Shelves: stuck (Not sure what to do next), jobs (Job by job: is it for me, how to get in, where it's heading), career-change (Changing careers), layoffs (After a layoff or redundancy), ai (AI, jobs and the future of work), job-search (Job searching and being found), applying (CVs, resumes, cover letters and applications), interviews (Interviews, offers and pay), work-life (At work: starting, leaving, rights and ways of working), students (Students, graduates and first jobs). Without a topic it lists the shelves with how many guides each holds.

topic.description: A shelf id such as 'applying' or 'layoffs', or a few words about the subject.

tools.name: get_career_direction
tools.description: Returns everything OffLadder holds on one emerging direction of work: what the days contain, why it is appearing now, what AI changes about it, the human abilities it leans on, the experience it grows out of, one small test and what is still unknown. Without a name, lists all 24 directions by family with one line each. Fits questions about what a newer kind of job involves, or requests for a list of emerging careers, e.g. 'what does a robot fleet supervisor do', 'what is an AI workflow designer', 'jobs in energy retrofit', 'list emerging careers', 'what new jobs exist in climate and energy', 'careers in AI that aren't engineering'.

name.description: The direction's name or a close description, e.g. 'digital accessibility engineer'. Leave out to list them all.

tools.name: look_up_job
tools.description: Looks up one named job or profession and returns everything OffLadder has written about it, for someone worried about their own job or weighing one to move into, e.g. 'will AI replace accountants', 'is my job as a paralegal safe from AI', 'will AI take software engineering jobs', 'is graphic design a dying career', 'what is the outlook for veterinarians', 'is nursing right for me', 'is cybersecurity a good career', 'how do I become an electrician', 'how to become a nurse practitioner', 'what can teachers do instead of teaching', 'careers after leaving law'. Covers 228 jobs across health, tech and data, finance, creative work, the trades, science, education and public service. For each job it returns the guides that exist: whether the work suits you and how to try it, how people get in, where the job is heading, what AI changes in it (which tasks are being automated and which stay with people), and what people move on to. Each guide comes with its direct answer, key points and primary sources such as the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, the International Labour Organization and the World Economic Forum. Says plainly when OffLadder has not written about a job. Does not list open vacancies or what a named employer pays, and never gives a percentage chance of replacement or a made-up forecast.

job.description: The job, profession or field, in the person's words, e.g. 'accountant' or 'graphic design'.

about.description: What they want to know: 'ai' (what AI changes in the job), 'future' (where the job is heading), 'fit' (whether it would suit them), 'route' (how to get in) or 'leaving' (what to do after it). Left out, every guide on the job comes back.

tools.name: compare_jobs
tools.description: Puts two or three named jobs side by side for someone choosing between them, e.g. 'nursing or teaching', 'should I become an electrician or a plumber', 'data analyst vs software engineer', 'physician assistant vs nurse practitioner', 'UX design or product management', 'accountant vs financial analyst, which is safer from AI', 'which is a better career, law or medicine'. For each job, returns what OffLadder has written about it across 228 jobs: whether the work would suit them and how to try it, how people get in, where it is heading and what AI changes in it, each with its direct answer and a link. Says which of the jobs it has nothing on. It does not rank the jobs or pick one: the comparison is for the person to weigh, and the suggested next step is a small test of each.

jobs.description: The two or three jobs to compare, each in the person's words, e.g. ['nurse', 'teacher'].

tools.name: browse_jobs
tools.description: Lists the jobs OffLadder has written about in one field of work, for someone who wants ideas or wants to see what exists before choosing one, e.g. 'what jobs are there in healthcare besides being a doctor', 'list careers in tech', 'what trades could I go into', 'creative jobs I could look at', 'public service careers', 'jobs in education that aren't teaching', 'what kinds of jobs are there'. Fields: health (Health and care), tech (Tech, data and AI), money (Business, office and finance), creative (Creative, media and design), trades (Trades, energy and transport), science (Science, engineering and land), public (Law, government and safety), education (Teaching and education), service (Service, hospitality and travel). Each job comes with what has been written about it (whether it suits you, how to get in, where it is heading, what AI changes, what people move on to) and a link. Without a field it lists the fields with how many jobs each holds. 228 jobs in all. It lists kinds of work, not open vacancies.

field.description: The field of work to list.

tools.name: plan_career_change_runway
tools.description: Works out how many months someone can afford to spend testing or making a career change, from their own numbers, e.g. 'can I afford to quit my job', 'how long can I last without a salary', 'I have 12,000 saved and spend 2,500 a month, how long do I have to change careers', 'how much runway do I need before I retrain', 'my severance is 20,000, how long before I need a job', 'can I afford to go part-time to study'. Takes savings or severance, essential monthly costs, any monthly income that continues, any one-off spend such as a course, and how many months of costs to keep untouched. Returns the number of months covered, the monthly gap, and a testing plan sized to that time. Pure arithmetic on the numbers given: it works in any currency, stores nothing, and is not financial advice.

savings.description: Money they could draw on: savings, severance or a payout. A plain number in the person's own currency.

monthly_costs.description: Essential monthly costs: housing, food, bills and debt repayments. A plain number in the person's own currency.

monthly_income.description: Money that would still come in each month: a job kept, part-time work, benefits or a partner's share. 0 if none. A plain number in the person's own currency.

one_off_costs.description: One-off spending on the change, such as a course or tools. 0 if none. A plain number in the person's own currency.

buffer_months.description: Months of costs to keep untouched as a safety buffer (default 1).

tools.name: start_my_reading
tools.description: For someone who doesn't know what to do next, feels stuck or lost about work, or wants help working out a direction, e.g. 'I feel lost in my career', 'I hate my job but don't know what else I'd do', 'help me figure out what to do with my life', 'I'm 35 and still don't know what I want', 'midlife career crisis', 'I just graduated and have no idea what to do'. Returns a link to OffLadder's four quick questions, plus one optional, with their starting world already picked, where OffLadder's coach suggests two directions and a first experiment. Worlds: build (I could build things), nature (I could work with nature), stories (I could tell stories), business (I could solve business problems), people (I could help people), systems (I could understand how things work).

world.description: The world that sounds closest to them, if clear.

hint.description: A few words about what they enjoy, used only to pick a world. Not stored.
